rows.title_short: Human Rights Compensation Act of 2004.\"
rows.abstract: \"Human Rights Compensation Act of 2004\".  The bill provides for compensation, free of tax, from the State to human rights violations (HRV) victims.  The amount of compensation shall be proportionate to the gravity of the human rights violations inflicted on the HRV victim.  It also provides for the creation of the Board of Compensation for Victims of Human Rights Violations under the Marcos Regime.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SAFETY MEASURES ON THE PRACTICE OF DENTAL MEDICINE, ENSURING ITS QUALITY AND STANDARD, INCREASING ITS PENALTIES THEREFROM, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 4419 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'PHILIPPINE DENTAL ACT OF 1965' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: To deter illegal dental practitioners from rendering dental services, the bill proposes certain safety measures to ensure the well being of the public. It increases penalties imposed on persons who practice dentistry without a certificate of registration from a fine of PhP3,000 to PhP5,000 and imprisonment of 1-5 years to a fine of PhP50,000 to PhP200,000 and imprisonment of 10-20 years.

rows.abstract: The bill extends to an overseas Filipino worker, with a valid contract certified by the POEA, a PhP50,000 loan from the OWWA to defray the living expenses of his family during the first few months of his absence and his expenses incurred during the pre-employment period.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2005-01-12

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO UPGRADE THE SALARY SCALE OF A RETIRING GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEE BY ONE GRADE FOR PURPOSES OF HIS/HER RETIREMENT
rows.abstract: The bill aims to offer a decent retirement benefit package to government personnel by upgrading the salary grade of a retiring employee by one grade on the date of his retirement. The upgraded salary scale shall then be used as the basis in computing the retirement benefits of the retiring employee.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D019
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09433) enacted on 2007-04-11
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA FOR SOCIAL WORKERS AND SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT WORKERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for Social Workers and Social Welfare and Development Workers
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Social Workers and Social Welfare and Development Workers\".  The highlights of the bill include:  a) the appointment of social workers in all social welfare and development agencies; b) payment for overtime work rendered; c) reasonable workload; d) entitlement to additional benefits; and e) promotion of their rights and privileges.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04536

rows.author: C122
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09344) enacted on 2006-04-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHESIVE JUVENILE JUSTICE SYSTEM AND DELINQUENCY PREVENTION PROGRAM, CREATING THE OFFICES OF JUVENILE JUSTICE AND DELINQUENCY PREVENTION; CHILDREN'S OMBUDSMAN, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to reform the present justice sytem and establish a comprehensive juvenile justice system. Provides for the exemption of minors from the penalties of crimes such as prostitution, mendicancy, vagrancy and curfew, among others; raises the age of criminal responsibility from nine to twelve years old and adheres to international standards concerning juvenile justice.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05065

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ANNUAL INCREASE OF THE AMOUNT OF PENSION PAID TO ALL RETIRED GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES BY AT LEAST AN AMOUNT EQUIVALENT TO THE RATED ANNUAL INCREASE IN THE NATIONAL LIVING INDEX AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The rising cost of living has made it increasingly difficult for retired government employees to provide for their family's daily sustenance from their monthly pension. The bill seeks to grant retirees an automatic increase in their pension equivalent to the annual rate of increase in the cost of living index.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL IRRIGATED AND IRRIGABLE AGRICULTURAL LANDS AS PROTECTED AREAS FOR AGRICULTURE, BANNING ITS CONVERSION FOR USES OTHER THAN AGRICULTURE, AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 20 OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE
rows.title_short: National Protected Areas for Agriculture (NPAA) Law
rows.abstract: \"National Protected Areas for Agriculture (NPAA) Law.\" The bill declares as National Protected Areas for Agriculture all irrigated agricultural lands planted with, but not limited to, rice, corn, sugar, coconut and other crops, blocked and mapped according to standards of the Bureau of Soils and Water. Such lands shall be non-negotiable for conversion to other uses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8794 OR 'AN ACT IMPOSING A MOTOR VEHICLE USERS' CHARGE ON OWNER OF ALL TYPES OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: The Road User's Tax Law is viewed to be regressive and untimely. This bill seeks the repeal of the law considering that motorists and other fuel users are already paying excise taxes on petroleum products.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A SPECIAL FUND FOR THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL RED CROSS BLOOD SERVICES
rows.abstract: The bill creates a special fund in the amount of P50.0 million which will be used by the Philippine National Red Cross Blood Services to ensure an adequate and safe supply of blood for charity patients. The fund shall be sourced from the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office, the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation and the National Treasury through the Department of Health.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING FIFTY (50%) PER CENTUM OF THE NATIONAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT'S SHARE IN ANY RECLAMATION PROJECTS TO PUBLIC EDUCATION
rows.abstract: The proposed 50% allocation from the share of the national and local government in any reclamation project shall be used for a) the acquisition of school sites; b) construction, repair, improvement and maintenance of school buildings; c) procurement of desks, tables, visual aids, books, computers; d) recruitment of teachers; and e) other essential requirements.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCENTIVES TO FILIPINOS WHO WILL TRAVEL TO DOMESTIC TOURIST DESTINATIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Local Travel Incentives Act
rows.abstract: \"Local Travel Incentives Act\".  The bill proposes the grant of incentives, such as discounts on transportation, accommodiation and meal expenses, to domestic tourists.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2004-08-02

rows.title_short: National Renewable Energy Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Renewable Energy Act of 2004.\" Promotes the production, commercialization and utilization of renewable energy systems using indigenous resources such as biomass, solar, wind, geothermal, hydro and ocean energy. rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164, BY EXTENDING THE TERM OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS INTO FIVE (5) YEARS
rows.abstract: The bill provides for the synchronization of barangay and sangguniang kabataan elections to be held on the last Monday of October 2007 and every five years thereafter. Further fixes the term of barangay and sangguniang kabataan officials to five years.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03742

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 99 AND 262 OR BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: RA 7166 failed to decriminalize acts with respect to persons making contributions to candidates and political parties. The bill seeks to remedy the situation by decriminalizing violations to Sections 98 and 99 of the Omnibus Election Code.  Nevertheless, it imposes on persons who violate these sections administrative fines similar to those provided in Section 14 of RA 7166 which are imposed on candidates and political parties who fail to file a report on campaign contributions and expenditures. In addition to the fines, a contributor who fails to comply with Sections 98 and 99 will not be able to claim exemption from donor's tax.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05877

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE MANDATORY LABELLING OF FOOD AND FOOD PRODUCTS CONTAINING GENETICALLY-MODIFIED ORGANISMS AND FOOD PRODUCED BY GENETIC ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGIES, AMENDING FOR THAT PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED AND TWENTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FOOD, DRUGS AND DRUG DEVICES AND COSMETICS ACT, AND REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-FOUR, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CONSUMERS' ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Genetically Engineered Food Right to Know Act
rows.abstract: Genetically Engineered Food Right to Know Act.\" Mandates all food and food products domestically sold, whether manufactured locally or imported, and which contain genetically modified organisms including those produced by genetic engineering technologies, to indicate such in the labels of their packaging followed by a government notice on the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D021
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE WORKERS' CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT TO SELF-ORGANIZATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Strengthening the Workers' Constitutional Right to Self-Organization
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to protect the rights of workers to self-organization by preventing undue interference and expediting the process of registration and certification of labor organizations. Allows rank and file and supervisory employees to join the same federation or national union, provides that the co-mingling of rank and file and supervisory employees in the same federation is not a ground for the cancellation of registration and encourages affiliation with federations and national unions.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT RA09481 (Lapsed into law on 2007-05-25)

rows.author: D021
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING GREATER PROTECTION TO LOCAL INDUSTRIES THROUGH THE IMPOSITION OF ANTI-DUMPING DUTY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 301, PART 2, TITLE II, BOOK 1 OF THE TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8752
rows.abstract: The bill deletes the provision in the Tariff and Customs Code of the Philippines which allows the Tariff Commission to decide whether or not to impose a definitive anti-dumping duty even when all the requirements for the imposition of said duty have been fulfilled. It further provides that 50% of the dumping duties collected from a particular dumping protest shall be returned to the petitioner.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D021
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER AND DATE OF ELECTION OF SECTORAL REPRESENTATIVES TO THE LOCAL SANGGUNIANS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Local Sectoral Representation Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Local Sectoral Representation Act of 2004.\" The bill provides for the election of three sectoral representatives each in the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang bayan and sangguniang panlungsod - one from the women sector, one from the workers and one from any of the following: the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons, and the elderly. Provides that the first election shall be held on the second Monday of May 2007 and every three years thereafter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D021
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2007-01-31, transmitted to on 2007-02-06 and received by the Senate on 2007-02-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING POLITICAL TURNCOATISM AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION SEVENTY-ONE OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. EIGHTY-EIGHT HUNDRED AND ONE, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: In order to minimize the politics of patronage and develop a strong multi-party system in the country, the bill provides the following penalties for political turncoatism: a) an elective official shall not be qualified to run for any elective position in any election immediately following the expiration of his term of office; b) a candidate, other than the incumbent elective official, shall not be qualified to run for any elective office immediately following his change of political party affiliation; and c) either of the above cases shall not be qualified to hold any elective office within the term of office immediately following the elections from which he was qualified.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05877

rows.author: D021
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09364) enacted on 2006-12-15
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 10 AND 53 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8223, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF MARIKINA FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING FOR TWO (2) CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICTS FOR THE CITY OF MARIKINA AND THE COMPOSITION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF MARIKINA
rows.status: Substituted by HB04078

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR AN OWWA CHARTER TO GOVERN THE OPERATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE OVERSEAS WORKERS WELFARE ADMINISTRATION, PRESCRIBE FOR PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE OWWA ADMINISTRATORS AND OFFICIALS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: OWWA Charter Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"OWWA Charter Act of 2004.\" To protect and promote the welfare of overseas Filipino workers, the bill seeks to provide for an OWWA Charter that will govern the operation and administration of the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration. It also prescribes for public accountability of the OWWA administrators and officials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2005-01-12

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR THE FILIPINO SEAFARERS
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for Filipino Seafarers
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Filipino Seafarers.\" The measure seeks to grant Filipino seafarers the following rights, among others: access to educational advancement and training; access to relevant information; humane conditions of work and to standard compensation; self-organization, collective bargaining and participation in democratic exercises; and legal representation. To expedite and simplify documentary processing, it provides for the establishment of the One-Step Center where concerned government agencies shall be represented.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2005-01-12

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA FOR THE WORKERS IN THE INFORMAL SECTOR, INSTITUTIONALIZING MECHANISM FOR IMPLEMENTATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for the Workers in the Informal Sector
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for the Workers in the Informal Sector.\" The bill seeks to extend government assistance, incentives and grants to accredited informal sector (IS) workers, and business acitivities or enterprises. Provides for the exemption of accredited IS workers/enterprises from all taxes, licenses and building permit fees. Also provides for the creation of the Informal Sector Development Council that will primarily be responsbile for the promotion, growth and development of the IS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2005-11-29, transmitted to on 2005-12-06 and received by the Senate on 2005-12-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING COUNTRYSIDE CREDIT THROUGH COOPERATIVE BANKS AND ENCOURAGING THE GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT OF COOPERATIVE BANKS BY AMENDING CHAPTER XIII OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6938, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill aims to strengthen the cooperative banking system, particularly in rural and remote areas. It extends to cooperative banks a similar package of incentives presently being enjoyed by thrift banks under RA 7906 and by rural banks under RA 7353.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04602

Committee Report Approved on 3rd Reading on Nov. 29, 2005 consolidated with HB Nos.699,1074,1123,1597,1954,2501,2915

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL HISTORICAL INSTITUTE'S (NHI) DOCUMENTATION SYSTEM ON PHILIPPINE LOCAL FOLK HISTORIES AND ORAL TRADITIONS, PROVIDING MECHANISM FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION, ALLOCATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Local Folk Histories Grant Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Local Folk Histories Grant Act of 2004.\" Establishes the National Historical Research Center which shall be tasked to monitor, implement, evaluate and approve matters pertaining to historical researches. Among its other functions, the Center shall advise and assist other agencies in the conduct of historical data-gathering and studies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RATIONALIZE THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF ALL LAWS ON OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH STANDARDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Under the present set-up, there are no less than 10 agencies involved in the implementation of occupational safety and health and environment protections laws. The measure designates the Department of Labor and Employment as the principal agency in coordinating and monitoring the government agencies involved in the implementation of all laws promoting occupation safety and health; and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources as the principal agency in the implementation of all laws on environmental protection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2007-02-19
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL TOURISM POLICY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: National Tourism Policy Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Tourism Policy Act of 2004.\" The bill proposes the adoption of the following policies, among others: a) encourage activities and programs which promote tourism awareness; b) promote the preservation of traditional crafts; c) encourage the use of indigenous architectural designs and materials; and d) grant preferential treatment to the employment of Filipinos.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06088

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING THE POTENTIALS OF THE FILIPINO YOUTH TOWARD NATION-BUILDING, PRESCRIBING THE FREE EXERCISE OF CERTAIN RIGHTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for the Youth
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for the Youth.\" Proposes to grant the youth the following rights: a) access to labor and employment; b) access to education; c) academic freedom; d) access to health care and services; e) free expression and information; f) organization and free assembly; g) paricipation in policy formulation; h) freedom of thought, conscience and religion; and i) political expression.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND NINE HUNDRED SIXTEEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE ACT OF 1995, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to strengthen the PEZA (Philippine Economic Zone Authority) Law by imposing stiffer requirements for those who will be nominated and appointed to manage the PEZA. The bill also ensures that appropriate and due compensation is given to persons or organizations affected and/or displaced by the establishment or expansion programs of the PEZA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, ARTS AND NATIONAL HERITAGE DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Department of Culture and National Heritage Act
rows.abstract:
\"Department of Culture and National Heritage Act.\"
The proposed department shall be mandated to: a) encourage the continuing development of our culture; b) conserve and promote the nation's historical and cultural heritage and resources; c) promote and disseminate patronage of our national culture and heritage; and d) preserve and integrate indigenous traditional culture into the mainstream of the dynamic culture of Filipinos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO UPGRADE THE POSITION TITLE AND SALARY GRADE OF STENOGRAPHIC REPORTER II (SG 6) AND STENOGRAPHIC REPORTER III (SG 11) TO STENOGRAPHIC REPORTER IV (SG 14), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Because of the increase in the number of cases being handled by the National Labor Relations Commissions, its stenographers are compelled to perform functions beyond their prescribed duties. To grant them equitable compensation and to correct the apparent misclassification of their positions, the bill proposes to upgrade the status of Stenographers Reporters II and III to Stenographic Reporter IV.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2005-02-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EARMARK TWENTY-FIVE (25%) PERCENT OF GOVERNMENT REVENUES ACCRUED FROM TOBACCO TAXES TO FUND TOBACCO CONTROL PROGRAMS AND ACTIVITIES OF THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: In recent years, several countries have decided to fund tobacco control activities through higher tobacco taxes. In like fashion, the bill provides that 25% of the revenues generated from tobacco taxes be allocated to fund tobacco control activities and broader public health programs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6963, ENTITLED 'AN ACT GRANTING SPECIAL FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE AND BENEFITS TO THE FAMILY OR BENEFICIARY OF ANY POLICE OR MILITARY PERSONNEL OR FIREMAN KILLED OR PERMANENTLY INCAPACITATED WHILE IN THE PERFORMANCE OF HIS DUTY OR BY REASON OF HIS OFFICE OR POSITION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The measure proposes the following: a) that the proceeds of the firearms license fees being collected by the Philippine Naitonal Police (PNP) Firearms and Explosives Office be allocated solely to the qualified dependents of the PNP; b) that educational benefits be extended to qualified dependents of non-uniformed personnel of the PNP; c) that the management of the educational funds for the dependents of the PNP be given to the PNP; and d) that the Chief, PNP, be authorized to use the educational funds for other purposes of the PNP.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FIELD OF LAND TITLE INSURANCE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 612 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INSURANCE CODE OF 1978, AS AMENDED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED 1455 AND 1460 AND BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 874
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to create a land title insurance system that would protect buyers of real estate against title defects, falsification, double titling and other similar unlawful acts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-08-02

rows.abstract: The bill prescribes the objectives/mission of the University, the composition of the Board of Regents, and the powers and duties of the Board and the University officials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-08-02

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-08-02

rows.author: E026
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 61 AND SECTION 103 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 856 OR OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'CODE ON SANITATION'
rows.abstract: The bill requires every cubicle in massage clinics and sauna bath estblishments to be adequately ventilated with sliding translucent curtains or transparent sliding glass doors without lock. It also limits the operating hours of massage and sauna bath parlors from 12 noon to 12 midnight and prohibits the use of use of display windows for masseurs and attendants.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-08-02

rows.author: E026
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING SQUATTING SYNDICATE, PROFESSIONAL SQUATTING AND LARGE-SCALE LAND GRABBING AS HEINOUS CRIMES, AND PROVIDING THE IMPOSITION OF DEATH PENALTY THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill provides for the imposition of the death penalty on squatting syndicates, professional squatters and manufacturers of fake land titles and other land related titles, and on land scale land grabbers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: E026
rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING THE PROVISIONS OF VAGRANCY AND AMENDING THE DEFINITION OF PROSTITUTES AS PROVIDED IN ARTICLE 202 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: The bill defines prostitutes as any person who, for money or profit, habitually indulges in sexual intercourse or lascivious conduct. Seeks the repeal of provisions on vagrancy under Paragraphs 1, 2, 3, and 4 of Article 202 of the Revised Penal Code.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: E026
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09482) enacted on 2007-05-25
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONTROL AND ERADICATION OF RABIES, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Anti-Rabies Act of 2002
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Rabies Act of 2002.\" The bill mandates the establishment of a National Rabies Prevention and Control Program which shall be a multi-agency effort to control and eradicate rabies in the country. Its activities shall include, among others, mass vaccination of dogs, impounding of stray dogs, and information and education campaign on the prevention and control of rabies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04654

rows.author: E026
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN AND PROPAGATE FOSTER CARE FOR ABANDONED, NEGLECTED AND OTHER CHILDREN WITH SPECIAL NEEDS, PROVIDING APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Foster Care Act of 2001
rows.abstract: \"Foster Care Act of 2001.\" The proposed act provides for a comprehensive legal farmework under which abused, neglected, surrendered, dependent and abandoned children can be provided with an alternative family. It seeks to systematize and enhance foster care in the country.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05525

rows.status: Substituted by HB06015

rows.author: D098
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 2, 3, AND 4 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 2000 ENTITLED, 'LIMITED ACCESS HIGHWAYS ACT'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to substitute any and all reference to the \"Department of Public Works and Communications\" in RA 2000 (Limited Access Highway Act) to the \"Department of Public Works and Highways.\"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D098
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 32 (h) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136 HEREBY REQUIRING THE MANDATORY COMPLIANCE BY ALL MOTORCYCLES TO AUTOMATICALLY TURN ON AND RIDE WITH THEIR HEADLIGHTS ON AT ALL HOURS OF THE DAY ON ALL ROADS
rows.title_short: Automatic Headlights on for Motorcycles Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Automatic Headlights On for Motorcycles Act of 2004.\" For the safety of all motorcycle drivers and passengers thereon and the commuting public, in general, all motorcycles are required to run on all roads with headlights turned on at all hours of the day. It requires motorcycle manufacturers to ensure that an automatic headlights on system is installed before sale.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-01-12

rows.author: D098
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 34 (h) OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4136 OR THEREBY REQUIRING THE MANDATORY COMPLIANCE BY ALL MOTORCYCLES OPERATORS, DRIVERS, RIDERS AND/OR PASSENGERS TO WEAR SAFETY HELMET
rows.title_short: Motorcycle Helmets Use Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Motorcycle Helmets Use Act of 2004.\" For the safety of motorcycle drivers and passengers, the bill provides for the mandatory use by motorists (drivers and passengers) of safety helmets of an approved type. The safety helmet shall be specifically designed to cushion and protect the rider's head from the impact of a crash.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-01-12
